error: AuthApiError: Invalid Refresh Token: Refresh Token Not Found
meaning: The browser had a saved Supabase session, but the refresh token in it is no longer valid on the server, so Supabase cannot renew the session. The user must sign in again.
causes: The user signed out elsewhere, or you reset their password / deleted the user.
Two tabs or two Supabase clients refreshed at the same time and one used an already-rotated token.
A session saved for a different Supabase project (e.g. you switched projects but kept the localStorage).
Server-side (Next.js) cookies not being updated after a refresh.

steps.text: Handle it gracefully: if getting the session fails, clear it and send the user to login.
steps.code:
const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
if (error) { await supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' }); router.push('/login') }

steps.text: Use one shared Supabase client instance in the browser; don't call createClient in multiple components.
In Next.js, use @supabase/ssr with the middleware from the Supabase docs so refreshed tokens are written back to cookies.
For yourself while testing: clear site data (DevTools > Application > Clear storage) after switching Supabase projects.

prompt: Users hit 'Invalid Refresh Token: Refresh Token Not Found' and get stuck. Ensure there is exactly one browser Supabase client, and on this error call supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' }) and redirect to /login instead of showing a broken page. If this is Next.js, set up @supabase/ssr middleware that refreshes and writes session cookies.

faq.a: No, it's Supabase correctly refusing an invalid token.
The old project's session stays in localStorage; the new project doesn't know its token.
